  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "f1",
      "concept_id": "c1",
      "text": "A checkpoint transfers content from the WAL file back into the original database file.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "A checkpoint operation takes content from the WAL file and transfers it back into the original database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f2",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "Each new connection defaults to an auto-checkpoint threshold of 1000 pages, subject to SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f3",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "For N > 0, sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) triggers a checkpoint after a transaction commits on any database of connection D if its WAL contains at least N frames.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "The sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(D,N) is a wrapper around sqlite3_wal_hook() that causes any database on database connection D to automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f4",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "Passing N <= 0 to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() disables automatic checkpoints on that connection.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f5",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "Checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() use SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are PASSIVE . Every new database connection defaults to having the auto-checkpoint enabled with a threshold of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT pages.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f6",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "The callback configured by sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint() and a custom sqlite3_wal_hook() callback replace one another.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "The callback registered by this function replaces any existing callback registered using sqlite3_wal_hook() . Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f7",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for database readers or writers to finish.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f8",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode. On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f9",
      "concept_id": "c5",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL checkpoints every WAL frame and syncs the database after waiting until there is no writer and all readers use the most recent database snapshot.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f10",
      "concept_id": "c5",
      "text": "While SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL is pending, it blocks new writers but allows new readers to proceed unimpeded.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f11",
      "concept_id": "c6",
      "text": "After checkpointing the WAL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART waits until all readers use only the database file, ensuring that the next writer restarts the WAL from its beginning.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f12",
      "concept_id": "c7",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE performs RESTART's steps and truncates the WAL to zero bytes just before a successful return.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f13",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP always checkpoints zero frames.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f14",
      "concept_id": "c9",
      "text": "A checkpoint must stop when it reaches a WAL page beyond any current reader's end mark.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f15",
      "concept_id": "c9",
      "text": "A checkpoint records progress in the wal-index so that the next invocation resumes from that position.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f16",
      "concept_id": "c10",
      "text": "Continuously overlapping readers can prevent checkpoint completion and cause unbounded WAL growth.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f17",
      "concept_id": "c10",
      "text": "Attempting checkpoints during reader gaps, when no process is reading the database, avoids the described checkpoint-starvation scenario.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are \"reader gaps\": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f18",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "A checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file unless journal_size_limit is set.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f19",
      "concept_id": "c17",
      "text": "An ongoing write transaction prevents WAL reset, allowing a large write transaction to produce a large WAL file.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction. So a large change to a large database might result in a large WAL file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f20",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before its content is transferred into the database.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f21",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f22",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only WAL operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f23",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "In the described synchronous=NORMAL configuration with checkpoints in a separate thread or process, transactions may roll back after a power failure or hard reset.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The downside to this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f24",
      "concept_id": "c13",
      "text": "Read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "On the other hand, read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f25",
      "concept_id": "c13",
      "text": "By default, the thread whose COMMIT pushes the WAL over its size limit runs the checkpoint.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f26",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "If another process is already checkpointing, checkpoint-lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f27",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE attempt to obtain the exclusive writer lock.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive \"writer\" lock on the database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f28",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "If the busy handler returns 0 before writer-lock acquisition or while waiting for readers, the checkpoint falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f29",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "When a blocked checkpoint falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE processing, it returns SQLITE_BUSY.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE - checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f30",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "For a successful call targeting one WAL database, a supplied pnLog output reports the total WAL frame count.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f31",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "For a successful call targeting one WAL database, a supplied pnCkpt output counts checkpointed frames cumulatively, including frames checkpointed before the call.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If pnCkpt is not NULL,then *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f32",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "A successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE targeting one WAL database sets the supplied pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to zero.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f33",
      "concept_id": "c16",
      "text": "If zDb is NULL or empty, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() attempts the operation on all WAL databases attached to the connection.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f34",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "When zDb is NULL or empty, the pnLog and pnCkpt output values are undefined.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db. In this case the values written to output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f35",
      "concept_id": "c16",
      "text": "For a named attached database outside WAL mode, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() returns SQLITE_OK and sets supplied pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to -1.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f36",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "By default, closing the last connection to a database triggers an automatic checkpoint.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "By default, SQLite will automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes.",
      "pass": 0
    }
  ],
  "passes": [
    {
      "pass": 0,
      "new_claims": 36,
      "total_claims": 36,
      "new_information_rate": 1.0
    }
  ],
  "handoffs": [],
  "verdict": "BOUNDED-STAGE",
  "limitations": [
    "All three supplied documents share the sqlite.org origin; they provide primary authority but do not satisfy a floor requiring independent origins.",
    "S1 lists only three checkpoint subtypes and mentions an undefined RESET; the dedicated S2 API reference governs the five supported mode names and semantics.",
    "S1 warns that RESTART/TRUNCATE may block readers, while S2 describes RESTART as not impeding readers and TRUNCATE as inheriting RESTART behavior; detailed mode scheduling follows S2.",
    "The packet does not establish checkpoint-mode introduction dates, independent performance benchmarks or external disagreements.",
    "One bounded extraction pass is reported; depth saturation has not been established."
  ]
}

claims.quote: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_NOOP This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.

claims.text: A checkpoint must stop when it reaches a WAL page beyond any current reader's end mark.
claims.quote: A checkpoint can run concurrently with readers, however the checkpoint must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader.

claims.text: A checkpoint records progress in the wal-index so that the next invocation resumes from that position.
claims.quote: The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.

claims.text: Continuously overlapping readers can prevent checkpoint completion and cause unbounded WAL growth.
claims.quote: However, if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.

claims.text: Attempting checkpoints during reader gaps, when no process is reading the database, avoids the described checkpoint-starvation scenario.
claims.quote: This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.

claims.text: A checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file unless journal_size_limit is set.
claims.quote: The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.

claims.text: An ongoing write transaction prevents WAL reset, allowing a large write transaction to produce a large WAL file.
claims.quote: the WAL file cannot be reset in the middle of a write transaction. So a large change to a large database might result in a large WAL file.

claims.text: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage before its content is transferred into the database.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database

claims.text: The database file must be synced before the WAL is reset.
claims.quote: The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.

claims.text: With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only WAL operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.
claims.quote: Note that with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).

claims.text: In the described synchronous=NORMAL configuration with checkpoints in a separate thread or process, transactions may roll back after a power failure or hard reset.
claims.quote: The downside to this configuration is that transactions are no longer durable and might rollback following a power failure or hard reset.

claims.text: Read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows.
claims.quote: On the other hand, read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content

claims.text: By default, the thread whose COMMIT pushes the WAL over its size limit runs the checkpoint.
claims.quote: By default, the checkpoint will be run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT that pushes the WAL over its size limit.

claims.text: If another process is already checkpointing, checkpoint-lock contention returns SQLITE_BUSY without invoking the busy handler.
claims.quote: If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned. Even if there is a busy-handler configured, it will not be invoked in this case.

claims.text: SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART and SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE attempt to obtain the exclusive writer lock.
claims.quote: The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive "writer" lock on the database file.

claims.text: If the busy handler returns 0 before writer-lock acquisition or while waiting for readers, the checkpoint falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE behavior.
claims.quote: If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE

claims.text: When a blocked checkpoint falls back to SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE processing, it returns SQLITE_BUSY.
claims.quote: the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE - checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.

claims.text: For a successful call targeting one WAL database, a supplied pnLog output reports the total WAL frame count.
claims.quote: If pnLog is not NULL, then *pnLog is set to the total number of frames in the log file

claims.text: For a successful call targeting one WAL database, a supplied pnCkpt output counts checkpointed frames cumulatively, including frames checkpointed before the call.
claims.quote: If pnCkpt is not NULL,then *pnCkpt is set to the total number of checkpointed frames in the log file (including any that were already checkpointed before the function was called)

claims.text: A successful SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE targeting one WAL database sets the supplied pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to zero.
claims.quote: Note that upon successful completion of an SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_TRUNCATE, the log file will have been truncated to zero bytes and so both *pnLog and *pnCkpt will be set to zero.

claims.text: If zDb is NULL or empty, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() attempts the operation on all WAL databases attached to the connection.
claims.quote: If parameter zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db.

claims.text: When zDb is NULL or empty, the pnLog and pnCkpt output values are undefined.
claims.quote: zDb is NULL or points to a zero length string, then the specified operation is attempted on all WAL databases attached to database connection db. In this case the values written to output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt are undefined.

claims.text: For a named attached database outside WAL mode, sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() returns SQLITE_OK and sets supplied pnLog and pnCkpt outputs to -1.
claims.quote: If database zDb is the name of an attached database that is not in WAL mode, SQLITE_OK is returned and both *pnLog and *pnCkpt set to -1.

claims.text: By default, closing the last connection to a database triggers an automatic checkpoint.
claims.quote: By default, SQLite will automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes.
